questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'Fear of confined spaces'
questions.x: 'Claustrophobia' means fear of confined spaces.

questions.q: No sooner did the bell ring ____ the students rushed out.
questions.x: 'No sooner…than' is the correct correlative.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
She is one of those / who always speaks / the truth.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'who always speaks'. The relative pronoun refers to 'those' (plural): 'who always speak'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
We have / less employees / than last year.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'less employees'. 'Employees' is countable: 'fewer employees'.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Lucid'.
questions.x: 'Lucid' means clear. 'Confusing' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To go back to the drawing board'
o: To start planning again after a failure
questions.x: 'To go back to the drawing board' means: to start planning again after a failure.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'Under the weather' mean?
questions.x: 'Under the weather' means: feeling unwell.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Eminent'.
questions.x: 'Eminent' means distinguished. 'Obscure' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Rejuvenate'.
questions.x: 'Rejuvenate' is the opposite of 'Exhaust'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Rejuvenate'.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A remedy for all diseases or problems'
questions.x: 'Panacea' means a remedy for all diseases or problems.

questions.q: According to the passage, what makes cooperatives succeed?
questions.x: Answer: 'Members' sense of ownership'. The first sentence makes this point. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Cooperatives succeed when members feel they own the enterprise, not merely use it. In the dairy cooperatives of western India, farmers elect their own leaders, receive payments based on the quality of milk and share in surpluses. This sense of ownership encourages them to supply consistently and to resist selling to private traders for a small premium. Where cooperatives have been captured by a few powerful families, the same farmers lose interest quickly.

questions.q: What happens when a few powerful families capture a cooperative?
questions.x: Answer: 'Farmers lose interest'. The last sentence says farmers lose interest. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Cooperatives succeed when members feel they own the enterprise, not merely use it. In the dairy cooperatives of western India, farmers elect their own leaders, receive payments based on the quality of milk and share in surpluses. This sense of ownership encourages them to supply consistently and to resist selling to private traders for a small premium. Where cooperatives have been captured by a few powerful families, the same farmers lose interest quickly.

questions.q: The Royal Indian Navy mutiny broke out in Bombay — this happened in the year:
questions.x: The Royal Indian Navy mutiny broke out in Bombay in 1946. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Who among the following was associated with the 'Self-Respect Marriage' and the Justice Party?
questions.x: Correct answer: E. V. Ramasamy (Periyar). Periyar later formed the Dravidar Kazhagam (1944).

questions.q: Aruna Asaf Ali is remembered for:
o: Hoisting the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank on 9 August 1942
questions.x: Correct answer: Hoisting the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank on 9 August 1942. She was called the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Independence movement.

questions.q: During the Quit India Movement, Usha Mehta is remembered for:
questions.x: Correct answer: Running the underground Congress Radio. The secret radio operated from Bombay.

questions.q: The boundary commission that demarcated the borders of India and Pakistan was headed by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Cyril Radcliffe. The Radcliffe Line awards were announced on 17 August 1947.

questions.q: Who gave Gandhi the title 'Mahatma'?
questions.x: Bose was the first to call him 'Father of the Nation' in a 1944 radio address.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian National Army:
1. It was revived by Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore.
2. Its slogan was 'Dilli Chalo'.
3. It reached Imphal and Kohima in 1944.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct; the INA campaign reached the Imphal–Kohima front in 1944.

questions.q: The women's regiment of the INA was named after:
questions.x: Correct answer: Rani Lakshmibai. It was led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (Sehgal).

questions.q: The 1906 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Calcutta; it was the session that adopted 'Swaraj' as the goal.

questions.q: The Doctrine of Lapse, a cause of resentment before 1857, was applied most aggressively by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Lord Dalhousie. Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur and Sambalpur were annexed under it.

questions.q: 'Garba' of Gujarat was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in:
questions.x: Correct answer: 2023. Kolkata's Durga Puja was inscribed in 2021 and Kumbh Mela in 2017.

questions.q: Which grouping became a permanent member of the G20 during India's presidency in 2023?
questions.x: Correct answer: African Union. The EU was already a member.

questions.q: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for:
o: Foundational discoveries enabling machine learning with artificial neural networks
questions.x: Correct answer: Foundational discoveries enabling machine learning with artificial neural networks. Their work underlies modern AI.

questions.q: India won how many medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games (held in 2023)?
questions.x: Correct answer: 107. It was India's best-ever tally, including 28 gold medals.

questions.q: 'Demographic dividend' can turn into a 'demographic disaster' if:
o: The working-age population is not adequately educated, skilled and employed
questions.x: Correct answer: The working-age population is not adequately educated, skilled and employed. Jobs and skills are critical to reaping the dividend.

questions.q: The 'Summit of the Future' (September 2024), which adopted the 'Pact for the Future', was held at:
questions.x: It included a Global Digital Compact and a Declaration on Future Generations.

questions.q: The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative aims to:
o: Enable women in self-help groups to earn at least ₹1 lakh a year
Provide loans of ₹1 lakh to women entrepreneurs only in cities
Give women ₹1 lakh as a gift
questions.x: Correct answer: Enable women in self-help groups to earn at least ₹1 lakh a year. The target was raised to three crore Lakhpati Didis.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. National Science Day marks C. V. Raman's discovery of the Raman effect.
2. National Mathematics Day honours Srinivasa Ramanujan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
Science Day is 28 February; Mathematics Day is 22 December.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 11 July?
questions.x: 11 July is World Population Day.

questions.q: Jay Shah took charge as Chairman of which body in December 2024?
questions.x: Correct answer: International Cricket Council. He is the youngest ICC chairman.

questions.q: "Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha" is the subject matter of which Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.x: It is the Fourth Schedule.

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office for:
o: At the pleasure of the President
Six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
questions.x: Correct answer: Six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier. He can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.

questions.q: The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on:
questions.x: Correct answer: 28 January 1950. It succeeded the Federal Court of India.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right after the 44th Amendment?
questions.x: Correct answer: Right to property. Property became a legal (constitutional) right under Article 300A.

questions.q: Citizenship in India is regulated by:
o: The Citizenship Act, 1955 (with Articles 5–11 of the Constitution)
questions.x: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 and its rules notified in March 2024 relate to persecuted minorities from three neighbouring countries.

questions.q: A proclamation of national emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within:
questions.x: It must be approved by a special majority; approval is valid for six months at a time.

questions.q: Which of the following States has a bicameral legislature?
questions.x: Six States have Legislative Councils: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Article 46 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
Promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections
Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
questions.x: Article 46: Promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections.

questions.q: Article 30 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Procedure for impeachment of the President
Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
Power of Parliament to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest
Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights
questions.x: Article 30: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.

questions.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms). Lord Minto has been called the 'father of communal electorate'.

questions.q: The India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement was signed in:
questions.x: It cuts tariffs on most Indian exports and provides for a Double Contribution Convention on social security for temporary workers.

questions.q: The R. N. Malhotra Committee (1994) is associated with:
o: Revising and strengthening the monetary policy framework
questions.x: R. N. Malhotra Committee (1994): Reforms in the insurance sector.

questions.q: The Union Budget 2025–26 set a fiscal deficit target of:
questions.x: Correct answer: 4.4% of GDP. The revised estimate for 2024–25 was 4.8% of GDP.

questions.q: Under the revised MSME classification announced in the Union Budget 2025–26, a 'micro' enterprise has investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to:
questions.x: Small: investment ≤ ₹25 crore and turnover ≤ ₹100 crore; medium: ≤ ₹125 crore and ≤ ₹500 crore.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹3,51,400 crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹2,51,000 crore. The GDP deflator is:
questions.x:
GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 = (3,51,400 / 2,51,000) × 100 = 140.
Prices have risen 40% over the base year.

questions.q: Soil Health Cards provide farmers with:
o: Crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilisers based on soil tests
questions.x: Correct answer: Crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilisers based on soil tests. The scheme was launched in 2015.

questions.q:
In which year did the following happen?
NABARD was established.
questions.x: NABARD was established in 1982.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Banks must maintain a Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
Reason (R): SLR ensures that banks hold liquid assets such as government securities to meet obligations.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains the purpose of SLR.

questions.q: 'Financial inclusion' primarily means:
o: Access to affordable financial services for all sections, especially the poor
questions.x: Correct answer: Access to affordable financial services for all sections, especially the poor. PMJDY is a major financial inclusion programme.

questions.q:
Match the organisation with its headquarters:
Organisation:
A. International Monetary Fund
B. World Trade Organization
C. Asian Development Bank
D. New Development Bank (BRICS)
Headquarters:
1. Geneva
2. Manila
3. Shanghai
4. Washington DC
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (International Monetary Fund) → 4 (Washington DC); B (World Trade Organization) → 1 (Geneva); C (Asian Development Bank) → 2 (Manila); D (New Development Bank (BRICS)) → 3 (Shanghai).
The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank is in Beijing; the World Bank is also in Washington DC.

questions.q: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are issued by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: International Accounting Standards Board (IASB). Ind AS are converged with IFRS; FASB issues US GAAP.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 100 units @ ₹18; 10th — 300 units @ ₹22; 20th — 200 units @ ₹25. 150 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 450 units left come from the latest purchases: 200 × ₹25 + 250 × ₹22 = ₹10,500.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹16,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹6,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹2,500; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹350. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹16,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 6,000
− Cheques deposited not credited 2,500
− Bank charges 350
Pass book balance = ₹19,150.

questions.q: Goods worth ₹5,000 destroyed by fire, fully uninsured, are recorded as:
o: Cash A/c Dr. To Loss by Fire A/c
Purchases A/c Dr. To Loss by Fire A/c
Loss by Fire A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c
Insurance Company A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c
questions.x: The loss is a nominal account debited; purchases are credited. If insured, the insurer would be debited for the admitted claim.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹3,40,000 is depreciated at 15% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 3,40,000 × (0.85)^3 = ₹2,08,802.50.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹1,87,000.)

questions.q: A product sells at ₹175 with a variable cost of ₹150 per unit. Fixed costs are ₹25,000. The break-even sales (in ₹) are:
questions.x:
P/V ratio = Contribution/Sales = 25/175 = 14.29%.
BEP sales = Fixed cost / P/V ratio = 25,000 / 0.1429 = ₹1,75,000.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹6,000 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 12% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 6,000 = ₹72,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 72,000 × 12% × 6/12 = ₹4,320.

questions.q: A 'marshalling' of the balance sheet refers to:
o: The order in which assets and liabilities are arranged (liquidity or permanence)
questions.x: Companies follow Schedule III order; sole traders may use liquidity or permanence order.

questions.q: A debit balance in the pass book indicates:
questions.x: In the pass book the bank records the customer's deposits as credits; a debit balance means overdraft.

questions.q: Which depreciation method can never reduce the asset's book value to zero?
questions.x: Correct answer: Written Down Value method. A fixed percentage of a declining balance never reaches zero.

questions.q: The profits of a firm for the last 4 years were ₹77,000, ₹34,000, ₹64,000, ₹79,000. Goodwill is to be valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit. Goodwill is:
Under the imprest system of petty cash:
o: A fixed amount is given once a year
The petty cashier is reimbursed the exact amount spent so that the float is restored
All payments are made by cheque
questions.x: Correct answer: The petty cashier is reimbursed the exact amount spent so that the float is restored. The imprest system keeps the opening float constant each period.

questions.q: Dividing the life of a business into equal periods (usually a year) for reporting follows the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Accounting period concept. Periodic statements allow measurement of profit and position.

questions.q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹3,45,000 and at the end ₹3,60,000. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹10,000 and withdrew ₹10,000 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 3,60,000 + 10,000 − 10,000 − 3,45,000 = ₹15,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: The EPFO's monthly 'payroll data', published since 2018, is mainly an indicator of:
o: Formal sector employment through net new EPF subscribers
questions.x: EPFO payroll data tracks new members joining, exits and rejoining, used as a proxy for formal employment.

questions.q: Prior permission of the appropriate government for lay-off, retrenchment and closure is required under the IR Code in industrial establishments employing at least:
questions.x: Chapter X applies to establishments (factories, mines, plantations) with 300 or more workers; the government may raise this threshold by notification.

questions.q: The right to form associations or unions is guaranteed under:
questions.x: Article 19(1)(c) guarantees the right to form associations or unions and (after the 97th Amendment) co-operative societies.

questions.q: The Hawthorne experiments (1924–32), which laid the foundation of the human relations school, were conducted at:
questions.x: Elton Mayo and colleagues found that social and psychological factors influence productivity.

questions.q: Bonus under the Code on Wages must ordinarily be paid within what period from the close of the accounting year?
questions.x: Bonus is payable within eight months from the close of the accounting year (unless the period is extended).

questions.q: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 prohibits employment of children below 14 years in:
o: All occupations and processes, except helping family enterprises after school hours and as child artists
questions.x: The 2016 amendment imposed a complete ban below 14 (with narrow exceptions) and prohibited adolescents (14–18) in hazardous occupations; the Act was renamed accordingly.

questions.q: Joint Management Councils (JMCs) in India were introduced on the recommendation of the:
questions.x: JMCs were introduced in 1958 as a voluntary scheme of workers' participation in management.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, the provisions on standing orders apply to industrial establishments with how many workers?
questions.x: The threshold was raised from 100 (under the 1946 Act) to 300 workers.

questions.q: In Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984), the Supreme Court dealt primarily with:
o: Release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers in stone quarries
questions.x: The PIL concerned bonded labourers in quarries near Delhi; the Court issued wide directions under Article 32.

questions.q: Under the Labour Codes, offences punishable only with fine may generally be:
o: Compounded, typically by paying a prescribed share of the maximum fine
Ignored if the employer is an MSME
Tried only by a Sessions Court
questions.x: The Codes introduce compounding of fine-only offences (commonly at 50% of the maximum fine) to decriminalise minor violations.

questions.q: The Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Cess is levied at a rate of:
o: Not less than 1% and not more than 2% of the cost of construction
questions.x: The cess, collected for welfare of construction workers, is between 1% and 2% of the cost of construction incurred by employers; the Code on Social Security retains this.

questions.q: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS), whose report highlighted that 'about 77% of Indians live on less than ₹20 a day', was chaired by:
questions.x: The Arjun Sengupta Commission (2004–09) studied the unorganised sector and recommended social security legislation.

questions.q: The International Social Security Association (ISSA), of which EPFO and ESIC are members, was founded in 1927 and is headquartered in:
questions.x: ISSA was founded under the auspices of the ILO and is based at the ILO in Geneva.

questions.q: Henri Fayol's principle of 'unity of command' means that:
o: Authority should be concentrated in one person
An employee should receive orders from only one superior
Each department should have one plan
All employees should work for a common goal
questions.x: Unity of command avoids conflicting instructions; 'unity of direction' means one head and one plan for activities with the same objective.

questions.q: The OSH Code applies to 'plantations' which, as defined, include those with at least:
questions.x: Plantations of five hectares or more with ten or more workers are covered; States may extend coverage to smaller ones.

questions.q: A worker's normal daily wage is ₹800 for an 8-hour day. For 3 hours of overtime under the Code on Wages, the worker must be paid at least:
questions.x: Hourly rate = 800/8 = ₹100; overtime at twice = ₹200/hour; 3 hours = ₹600.

questions.q: The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 required the Central Government to formulate schemes for unorganised workers on matters including:
o: Life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits and old-age protection
questions.x: The Act listed these areas (Schedule I schemes such as RSBY, IGNOAPS, PMJJBY-type covers).

questions.q: The PFRDA Act was passed in:
questions.x: The PFRDA Act, 2013 (effective February 2014) gave statutory backing to the regulator set up in 2003.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the three schemes framed under the EPF & MP Act, 1952?
o: EPF Scheme 1952, EPS 1995 and EDLI Scheme 1976
questions.x: EPFO administers three schemes: Provident Fund (1952), Deposit-Linked Insurance (1976) and Pension (1995).

questions.q: Medical benefit under the ESI scheme is available to:
o: The insured person and family members from the first day of insurable employment
Only the insured person after one year
questions.x: Full medical care is provided to the insured person and dependants from day one.

questions.q: The world's first national social insurance system, starting with sickness insurance in 1883, was introduced in Germany by:
questions.x: Bismarck introduced sickness (1883), accident (1884) and old-age and invalidity insurance (1889).

questions.q: 'One Rank One Pension' (OROP) for defence pensioners was implemented in:
questions.x: OROP ensures the same pension for the same rank and same length of service irrespective of retirement date.

questions.q: Under the Supreme Court's 2022 judgment on EPS, members eligible for 'higher pension' could opt to contribute on:
o: Actual salary above the wage ceiling
questions.x: Eligible members who were in service on or after 1 September 2014 were allowed to opt for pension on actual wages.

questions.q: An insured employee earns gross wages of ₹10,000 in a month. What is the total ESI contribution (employer + employee) payable for that month?
questions.x:
Employee share 0.75% = ₹75 → ₹75; employer share 3.25% = ₹325 → ₹325 (rounded up to the next rupee).
Total = ₹400 (4% of wages; rates in force since 1 July 2019).

questions.q: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT), EPF is chaired by:
o: The Union Minister for Labour and Employment
questions.x: The CBT is tripartite; the Labour Minister is Chairman and the Central PF Commissioner is the chief executive.

questions.q: EPS 1995 replaced which earlier scheme?
questions.x: The Family Pension Scheme of 1971 was replaced by EPS 1995, which provides both member and family pension.

questions.q: Brazil's 'Bolsa Família' is an example of a:
questions.x: It gives cash to poor families conditioned on children's schooling and health.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹11,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹11,000 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 20%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 11,000) = ₹11,000.
Salary for computation = min(11,500, 11,000) = ₹11,000.
Annual bonus = 11,000 × 12 × 20% = ₹26,400. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: Heat transfer from the Sun to the Earth takes place by:
questions.x: Radiation does not need a medium.

questions.q: A geostationary satellite orbits the Earth at an altitude of about:
questions.x: Its period equals one day, so it appears stationary over a point on the equator.

questions.q: Loss of water as vapour from the aerial parts of plants is called:
questions.x: Correct answer: Transpiration. It occurs mostly through stomata.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to select all content in most applications?
questions.x: Correct answer: Ctrl + A. Ctrl + E and Ctrl + L align text in MS Word.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Xylem carries water from roots to leaves.
2. Phloem carries food prepared in leaves to other parts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Correct answer: Both 1 and 2. Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
Both are correct.

questions.q: A 'firewall' is used to:
o: Monitor and control network traffic based on security rules
questions.x: Correct answer: Monitor and control network traffic based on security rules. It can be hardware or software.

questions.q: In PowerPoint, which view shows thumbnails of all slides for rearranging?
questions.x: Correct answer: Slide Sorter view. Slide Sorter helps reorder slides.

questions.q: The process of coating iron with zinc to prevent rusting is called:
questions.x: Correct answer: Galvanisation. Vulcanisation hardens rubber with sulphur.

questions.q: N₂O (nitrous oxide) is commonly known as:
questions.x: N₂O (nitrous oxide) is laughing gas.

questions.q: Electron is credited to:
questions.x: Electron: J. J. Thomson.

questions.q: Which of the following is a programming language?
questions.x: HTML is a markup language rather than a general-purpose programming language.

questions.q: Most digestion and absorption of food take place in the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Small intestine. Villi increase the surface area for absorption.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 5, 6, 10, 19, 35, ?
questions.x: Differences are 1², 2², 3², 4² (1, 4, 9, 16). Next difference = 5² = 25 → 35 + 25 = 60.

questions.q: A box contains 8 red, 4 blue and 2 green tokens. Two tokens are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.x:
Ways to choose 2 red = C(8,2) = 28; ways to choose any 2 = C(14,2) = 91.
P = 28/91 = 4/13.

questions.q: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 20 years. In how many years will it become 5 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 20 years, i.e. rate = 100/20 = 5% p.a.
To become 5 times, interest must be 4 × principal.
Time = (4 × 100) / 5 = 80 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 50% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. His gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Let CP = 100. Marked price = 150.
SP after 15% discount = 150 × 0.85 = 127.5.
Gain = 127.5 − 100 = 27.5 on 100 → 27.5% gain.
Shortcut: m − d − md/100 = 50 − 15 − 7.5 = 27.5%.

questions.q: In a certain code language, FACTOR is written as JWGPSN. How is MINES written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare FACTOR → JWGPSN: F→J, A→W, C→G…
Rule: letters in odd positions move 4 forward and letters in even positions move 4 backward.
Applying it to MINES gives QERAW.

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 361, 625, 900 and 901.
questions.x: 900, 625, 361 are all perfect squares; 901 is not. Hence 901 is the odd one out.

questions.q: If A : B = 4 : 2 and B : C = 6 : 4, and a sum of ₹9,900 is shared among A, B and C in that combined ratio, C receives:
A invests ₹35,000 for the whole year and B invests ₹55,000 after 8 months. If the annual profit is ₹16,000, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 35,000×12, B: 55,000×4 → 21 : 11.
B's share = 11/32 × 16,000 = ₹5,500.

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word 'PENSION' be arranged so that all the vowels always come together?
questions.x:
Vowels: E, I, O; consonants: P, N, S, N.
Treat the vowels as one block → 5 units → 60 arrangements (N appears 2 times).
Vowels inside the block: 6 ways (all letters are distinct).
Total = 60 × 6 = 360.

questions.q: Gita starts from point O and walks 15 km towards South, then turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right and walks 7 km, and finally turns right and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -15 +7 = -8 km → 8 km South.
East–West: -8 +14 = 6 km → 6 km East.
Distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 km, towards South-East.

The average age of 25 trainees in a batch is 14 years. When the instructor's age is also included, the average rises by 1.5 years. The instructor's age is:
questions.x:
Total of trainees = 25 × 14 = 350.
With instructor: 26 × 15.5 = 403.
Instructor = 403 − 350 = 53 years.

questions.q: A bus runs from town P to town Q at 24 km/h and returns along the same road at 72 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.x:
For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) (harmonic mean), not (u + v)/2.
= 2 × 24 × 72 / (24 + 72) = 3456/96 = 36 km/h.
